summary:
Selene is a Lunar Landing Navigator and Safety calculator. 
Users can choose a coordinate or enter a latitude and longitude on the 3d moon map and then enter the time range of the mission as a start date and end date. The app will calculate and find out which hours are best for the mission (hours with both solar energy from the Sun with no obstruction and direct communication with Earth).
details:
Selene Lunar Navigator

Selene is web based tool that can be used to gather data about lunar landing sites.

A landing site is optimal if

1. It has access to sunlight without obstruction

2. It has line of sight with Earth for communication

For a landing site to be completely optimal these two conditions have to be satisfied.

To calculate if a landing site is optimal to land Selene uses these information

- Start Date of the mission

- End Date of the mission (both of these act as the time period for calculations to take place within)

- Azimuth, Elevation of the Sun and Earth from the Moon (using the NASA JPL Horizon API)

- High precision 3D topographic maps of the Moon (using LOLA Maps from imbrium mit edu)

First the landing calculation takes both the Start and End dates to narrow the processing to the time range between these dates.

Then the calculation for two values namely POWER and COMMS take place.

POWER : Amount of sun visible | For solar energy required for mission

COMMS : Line of sight with Earth | Communication

Then the function calculates these values for each value in the time range and returns it. While doing the calculation both the LOLA map and Horizon API are used in tandem since for geometric surface calculations, the Horizon API effectively treats the Moon as a sphere, even though its underlying software framework uses a triaxial ellipsoid model.

The LOLA maps give some more accurate calculation in sites where the terrain obstructs sunlight.

This calculated data is returned to the frontend of Selene and is rendered as a 3d moon with the Sun and Earth at accurate positions based on the data.

The timeline at the bottom shows an overview of the data

Here the Optimal time range is where both comms and power is available Using the playhead users can view the path of the sun and earth in the 3d view.

On top of the web are the set of coordinates where the mouse cursor is currently hovering over, Users can also double click the coordinates to manually change the coordinates.

Below that is an arrow that is used to reveal the compare feature.

When the compare feature is selected, we have two options,
1. Compare two landing sites using the same timeline
or
2.Compare the same sight over two different timelines, the timelines should be of same length to have an accurate comparison

The comparison feature also shows which selected sample is more optimal(optimal sample are those samples which have maximum power and comms)

Another feature is to export all the data of selected sites(manually selected and preloaded named landmarks), the data will be exported in .json format.
